text:
morgan: Heads-up — we saw a sustained p95 jump (~45%) right after the variant swap completed (~01:07 UTC). A few customers hitting timeouts. Affected runtime version: v3.3.0 (rolled from v3.2.1).

deploy-bot: rollout finished: runtime-v3.3.0 -> 100% at 2026-03-15T01:07:10Z :rocket:

sre-oncall: copying dashboards/traces now. any request ids or customer examples you can paste here? which cohorts/models saw the worst delta?

morgan: sample req ids: req_0a12ef, req_0b22fc, req_0c33ad. cohort=payments-heavy, model=redwood-7b-quant. p95 before: ~120ms, after: ~175ms. p99 spikes to ~1.2s.

sam: can we check KV cache miss rates and batching distribution? rollout included a scheduler tweak earlier today, could be increasing wait time for small requests.

chris: I pulled the runtime diff — PR #4567 changed the soft-batch timeout from 5ms -> 15ms and adjusted the scheduler heuristic to prefer larger batches. That matches an increase in small-request tail.

alexa: also saw a quant-scheduler bump in v3.3.0 (commit 9f2b). It changes eager-eviction threshold for small KV entries. Might be auth/kvcache churn for tenants with many short chats.

jamie: ops concern: customers are seeing 5xx or slow 200s? any auth errors?

morgan: mostly 200s but long TTFB, a couple of 504s from the edge when we hit timeout. No auth errors in the samples.

sre-oncall: quick checks:
- q1: Are slow traces attributing time to scheduler WAIT or to token generation?
- q2: Did the kernel selector change (AVX/quant kernels) on canary hosts?
- q3: Any change in autoscaling smoothing or burst capacity?

sam: PromQL we used to quantify:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, runtime_version))
```
Split by runtime_version shows v3.3.0 p95 ~175ms, v3.2.1 p95 ~118ms.

chris: I want to repro locally with a payments-heavy synthetic: small short prompts at 20qps with KV cache warm/cold toggles. We'll run v3.2.1 and v3.3.0 with identical load.

morgan: customer impact is real; propose immediate mitigation: 1) rollback runtime for affected shard(s) to v3.2.1 2) force routing policy to prefer reserved capacity where possible 3) open a bisect-run to pinpoint change. Thoughts? :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: agree rollback for the shard is safest short-term. Chris — can you prepare a targeted rollback plan? Include canary to 5% then 100% per shard. I'll coordinate on-call handoff.

chris: rollback command (will run in prod ops):
```
# rollback runtime version on shard payments-prod-1
redwoodctl rollout set --shard payments-prod-1 --runtime-version v3.2.1 --strategy gradual --wait
```

ops-bot: rollback job queued: job_id=rb-20260315-001, initiated by chris, ETA ~3m.

morgan: applying rollback now to payments-prod-1. Will post p95 after it settles (give it ~4m).

(4m later)

morgan: update: after rollback p95 for payments-heavy cohort decreased from 175ms -> 122ms, p99 back to ~300ms. Customers reporting latency improvement. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: good. We'll keep rollback in place for the shard while we bisect. Chris/Sam — action items for root cause bisect:
- reproduce with synthetic requests (sam/chris).
- run two-axis test: (runtime v3.2.1 vs v3.3.0) x (soft-batch timeout 5ms vs 15ms) x (quant-scheduler old vs new).
- enable per-request tracing and attach timelines for slow requests.
- add sampling rule on payments-prod to collect 1% full traces for 1h.

sam: I'll kick off the synthetic runs and send logs + flamegraphs. Hypothesis: the scheduler heuristic change increases median wait for small requests under typical inter-arrival distribution, pushing p95 up.

chris: if synthetic repro confirms scheduler change is primary, options: revert scheduler change, tune soft-batch timeout back to 5ms, or implement traffic-aware adaptive timeout (shorter for small requests). We'll propose a config patch rather than a full runtime bump.

alexa: also want to correlate kvcache eviction metrics: `redwood_kvcache_evictions_total` spiked right after rollout. If eviction churn is high, cold KV loads can add ~20-50ms per request.

jamie: documentation note: add this scenario to the rollout playbook — when increasing batch wait time, include a phasing plan with small-request cohorts.

sre-oncall: for now: 1) keep rollback on payments-prod-1, 2) block global ramp of v3.3.0, 3) run bisect tests, 4) prepare a patch release to revert scheduler timeout if confirmed. I'll file an incident tracker and set priority P2 for follow-up.

morgan: incident created: INC-2026-0315-09. I'll paste links to dashboards and request logs in the ticket.

chris: starting canary reproducibility matrix now. I'll post results and attach traces. Thanks all for fast response.

morgan: thanks team — appreciate quick rollback. We'll keep this thread updated with bisect results and proposed config changes.

ops-bot: reminder: schedule postmortem sync in #eng-runtime tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
